title: CRJA/11/2018 of Roshan Singh Negi Vs State Of Uttarakhand

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Jail Appeal No. 11 of 2018
Roshan Singh Negi ......... Appellant
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand .......Respondent
Present:
Mr. Rajendra Arya, Amicus Curiae.
Mr. Lalit Miglani, A.G.A. for the State.
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
Present appeal is preferred against the judgment
and order dated 19.01.2016, passed in Sessions Trial No. 32
of 2015, State vs. Roshan Singh Negi, by the Additional
District and Sessions Judge, Kotdwar, District Pauri
Garhwal. By the impugned judgment and order, the
appellant has been convicted under Sections 376 (l) IPC and
sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of
ten year with a fine of Rs.2000/- In default of payment of
fine, to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of two
months.
2. Briefly stated, the facts are as hereunder:-
The victim in the instant case is a mentally
retarded woman. At the time of incident, she was 39 years of
age. She was staying in the village alongwith her aunt. Her

2
brother was working in Chandigarh. Her mother was unwell,
therefore, she used to visit her son in Chandigarh. The
mother of the victim noticed that the victim is pregnant. She
inquired as to whose child is she carrying. To it, the victim
told that the appellant forcibly raped her. The mother and
the aunt of the victim informed this fact to the brother of the
victim, who was staying in Chandigarh. He lodged an FIR
Ex. A1 on 25.07.2015 at the concerned Revenue Police
Station. A Crime No. 2 of 2015 was lodged against the
appellant. On 10.08.2015, the victim was medically
examined. She was 32 weeks pregnant then. She was
referred for medical treatment at the higher center. At the
time of medical examination, the foetus had already died.
The victim was then admitted at Himalayan Hospital,
Dehradun. She was admitted on 13.08.2015and discharged
on 16.08.2015. During this period, the Investigating Officer
(for short, "the IO") also tried to get the scientific evidence.
When the hospital authorities were not ready to take
samples for Deoxyribonucleic Acid ("DNA") examination. The
IO approached the concerned court. The concerned court by
communication Ex. A4 and A7 requested the concerned
medical authorities to take samples for DNA examination of
the foetus and the appellant respectively. Such samples
were taken. Forensic Science Laboratory ("FSL") report Ex.
A14 concluded that the appellant is biological father of the

3
foetus and the victim is biological mother of the foetus. The
Investigating Officer also prepared the site plan. The victim
was also examined under Section 164 of the Code of
Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short, "the Code") on
02.09.2015. After investigation, charge sheet Ex. A12 was
submitted against the appellant. On 24.11.2015, charge
under Section 376 and 506 IPC were framed against the
appellant.
3. In order to prove its case, prosecution examined
seven witnesses, namely, PW1, brother of the victim, PW2
the victim, PW3 aunt of the victim, PW4 Sub Inspector,
Vinod Kumar, PW5 Dr. Malti Yadav, PW6 Inspector Chandra
Mohan Joshi and PW7 Dr. Subhash Kumar.
4. The appellant was examined under Section 313 of
the Code. According to him, the witnesses have given a false
evidence against him. In order to grab his property, he has
been falsely implicated in the case.
5. Learned court below, after hearing the parties, by
the impugned judgment and order, convicted and sentenced
the appellant, as stated hereinbefore. Aggrieved by it, the
appeal is preferred.

4
6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused
the record.
7. Learned Amicus Curiae would submit following
two points in his statement:-
(i) FIR is delayed and;
(ii) The relationship between the appellant and
the victim were consensual.
8. It is submitted that, had the victim been raped by
the appellant, the victim would have at least complained
about it to her mother or aunt or any other person in the
village. But, she maintained silence for a long period and
after six months revealed it to her mother, which doubts the
credibility of the statements of the victim. Thereafter, FIR
has been lodged which is much delayed and it doubts the
prosecution case.
9. It is also submitted by learned Amicus Curiae
that, in fact, in her statement recorded under Section 164 of
the Code, the victim has told that the appellant would
brought her "Roti", tobacco and mangoes. On the basis of
this statement, it is submitted that it reflects as if a
relationship between the victim and the appellant were
consensual.

5
10. On the other hand, learned State counsel would
submit that the statement of the victim proves the case
against the appellant. The victim has categorically stated
that it is the appellant, who raped her. The victim is
mentally retarded woman. She is though capable to
understand things, but she is mentally retarded. Other
prosecution witnesses have also supported the prosecution
case. Learned State counsel would submit that in the
instant case, the scientific evidence concludes the guilt of
the appellant. The DNA examination has established that
the appellant was biological father and the victim was
biological mother of the foetus.
11. In the instant case, the FIR was lodged by the
brother of the victim, who has been examined as PW1.
According to him, his sister is mentally retarded. This
witness was on the job in Chandigarh. The victim was
staying in the village along with her aunt. Since the victim
was mentally retarded, she was not married. She used to do
all household works. She would go in forest with the
animals for grazing. According to this witness, on
25.07.2015, he was in the village when he was told by his
mother and aunt that the appellant raped the victim forcibly
and he did it twice, once in the shrubs and second time in
her house. When the mother of the victim noticed her
pregnancy, she inquired, it is thereafter, the victim revealed

6
that the appellant raped her. The appellant also threatened
the victim to life, in case, she would reveal the incident to
anyone. This witness has also stated that, in fact, the
appellant is the person with criminal antecedents. He has
been in jail on various occasions in the case of molestation.
12. PW1 the brother of the victim would also state
that a disability certificate Ex. A2 of the victim. He also
states that the victim was examined in the court during
investigation and she put her thumb impression on it. He
also stated about the DNA examination of the foetus.
13. PW2 is the victim. Admittedly, the victim is
mentally retarded. The court questioned her generally.
Though, the questions and answers as such have not been
recorded, but the court has observed that the victim is
mentally retarded and she is not mentally fit, but still court
recorded her statement. In her examination, PW2 the victim
identified the appellant and named him. According to her,
once the appellant muffled her mouth, pulled her in the
shrubs and did galat kaam with her. Once again, according
to PW2, the victim, the appellant did galat kaam with this
witness in her house and due to this galat kaam, she
became pregnant. This witness has also stated that she has
given statement as recorded under Section 164 of the Code.

7
14. PW3 the aunt of the victim has corroborated the
statements of PW1, the brother of the victim and PW2 the
victim. She has categorically told that the mother of the
victim and this witness noticed that the victim is pregnant.
On inquiry made by them, the victim told them that it is the
appellant, the son of Sadhu, who raped her twice and
threatened her to life, in case, she would reveal it to anyone.
According to PW3, the aunt of the victim, the victim was
sent to Dehradun Hospital, where her foetus was removed,
which was dead.
15. PW4 Vinod Kumar is the Investigating Officer, he
has stated about the steps which he has taken during the
course of investigation. PW4 Vinod Kumar applied to the
court for taking DNA samples by the Hospital. Based on
which, according to this witness, the court concerned,
requested the medical authorities to take the samples for
DNA examination. Samples were so taken and deposited
under seal and signatures in the FSL. The victim was
examined under Section 164 of the Code. Site plan was
prepared and after completing investigation, this witness
submitted charge sheet Ex. A12. This witness has also
proved the FSL report Exs. A13, A14 and A15.

8
16. PW5 Dr. Malti Yadav medically examined the
victim on 10.08.2015. According to her, the victim was
anaemic She was mentally retarded and she was pregnant
for 32 weeks. The foetus was dead. Therefore, this witness
referred the victim to higher center. She proved the medical
examination report Ex. A16.
17. PW6 Chandra Mohan Joshi wrote the chik FIR
and made entries in the General Diary. He also proved these
documents.
18. PW 7 Dr. Subhash Kumar took the DNA samples
of the appellant, sealed it and handed over to the Police. He
also took the DNA samples of the victim. He proved these
documents.
19. The appellant has been convicted under Section
376 (2) (l) IPC. The victim is mentally retarded. The victim
has not been administered oath. What would be its
implication? How to appreciate the evidence of the victim?
First and foremost, it has to be examined.
20. Section 118 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 (for
short, "the Evidence Act"), makes provisions as to who may
testify. This Section is as hereunder:-

9
"118. Who may testify. -- All persons shall be competent
to testify unless the Court considers that they are prevented
from understanding the questions put to them, or from giving
rational answers to those questions, by tender years, extreme
old age, disease, whether of body or mind, or any other cause of
the same kind.
Explanation. -- A lunatic is not incompetent to testify,
unless he is prevented by his lunacy from understanding the
questions put to him and giving rational answers to them."
21. The explanation appended to Section 118 of the
Evidence Act, makes it abundantly clear that in fact a
lunatic would also be a competent witness unless he is
prevented by his lunacy from understanding the questions
put to him. Definitely in such cases, it would depend upon
the person who is a lunatic.
22. The provision of oath is given under the Oaths
Act, 1969 (for short, "the Act"). It is administered under
Section 4 of the Act. Section 7 of the Act, makes the
provision in case oath is not administered. According to it,
the evidence which is not on oath, does not become in
admissible. This Section reads as hereunder:-
"7. Proceedings and evidence no invalidated by
omission of oath or irregularity.- No omission to take
any oath or make any affirmation, no substitution of any
one for any other of them, and no irregularity whatever in
the administration of any oath or affirmation or in the
form in which it is administered, shall invalidate any
proceedings or render inadmissible any evidence
whatever, in or in respect of which such omission,

10
substitution or irregularity took place, or shall affect the
obligation of a witness to state the truth."
23. In the case of Sidhapal Kamala Yadav Vs. State of
Maharashtra, (2009) 1 SCC 124, the Hon'ble Supreme Court
observed that "there are four kinds of persons who may
be said to be non compos mentis (not of sound mind) i.e.
(1) an idiot; (2) one made non compos by illness; (3) a
lunatic or a mad man; and (4) one who is drunk. An idiot
is one who is of non-sane memory from his birth, by a
perpetual infirmity, without lucid intervals; and those
are said to be idiots who cannot count twenty, or tell
the days of the week, or who do not know their fathers
or mothers, or the like (see Archbold's Criminal
Pleadings, Evidence and Practice, 35th Edn., pp. 31-
32; Russell on Crimes and Misdemeanors, 12th Edn.,
Vol. 1, p. 105; 1 Hale's Pleas of the Crown 34). A person
made non compos mentis by illness is excused in
criminal cases from such acts as are committed while
under the influence of his disorder (see 1 Hale PC 30). A
lunatic is one who is afflicted by mental disorder only at
certain periods and vicissitudes, having intervals of
reason (see Russell, 12th Edn., Vol. 1, p. 103; Hale PC
31). Madness is permanent. Lunacy and madness are
spoken of as acquired insanity, and idiocy as natural
insanity."

11
24. In the case of Tulshidas Kanolkar Vs. State of
Goa, (2003) 8 SCC 590, the Hon'ble Supreme Court
considered the evidence of the mentally retarded victim of
rape and observed that "they asked the victim as to who
was responsible for her pregnancy. She in her own way
pointed out accusing fingers at the appellant and said
that on some pretext or the other, he ravished her.
When this shattering news was conveyed to the parents
of the victim, they questioned the appellant. It is on
record that some money was offered to them by the
mother of the appellant to have termination of
pregnancy."
25. In the case of Rameshwar Vs. The State of
Rajasthan, AIR 1952 SC 54, the Hon'ble Supreme Court
observed that the main purpose of administering oath to
render persons who give false evidence liable to prosecution
and the subsidiary object is to bring home to the witness the
solemnity of the occasion and to impress upon him the duty
of speaking the truth. Omission to take the oath does not
affect the admissibility of the evidence.
26. A lunatic is not incompetent to testify. What is
important is that his level of understanding has to be
assessed so as to ascertain his level of understanding the

12
questions put to him and giving rationale answer. Merely
because oath has not been administered, as stated, does not
make evidence inadmissible in view of Section 7 of the Act.
In view of this settled legal position, first and foremost, it
will be examined as to whether the victim was able to
understand the questions put to her and answer them
rationally.
27. The victim was examined during investigation
under Section 164 of the Code. In her statement given under
Section 164 of the Code, she has stated that the appellant
did galat kaam on two occasions, once in the shrubs and
once again in her house. He had muffled her mouth. In her
examination in the court, when she was questioned to
assess the level of understanding, the court has observed
that she is not able to reply some of the questions. The court
has not observed that the victim at all is not able to
understand the questions put to her. In fact, a certificate of
mental retardation given for Government benefits to the
victim reveals that she was 50% mentally retarded and it
was assessed as moderate. There is another level below it,
which is mild. There are two levels above it which are severe
and profound. This certificate itself reveals that the victim
was on the lower side of mental retarded people. She was in
the moderate category. The court has observed that she was
able to understand questions, but she was not able to

13
understand some of the questions. It establishes that, in
fact, the victim was able to understand the questions and
answers. This is, in fact, the factual analysis and it also
depends upon the question that might be asked from such
mentally retarded person.
28. Here is a case of rape. The victim, a woman of 39
years of age, living all alone in her village with her aunt tells
that she was raped. She became pregnant. In the court also,
the victim is categorical that she was raped twice by the
appellant. Once in the forest when the appellant muffled her
mouth and pulled her in the shrubs and second time,
according to PW2 the victim, she was raped by the appellant
in her own house. The victim was consistent in her
statement recorded under Section 164 of the Code also. She
has stated that she was raped twice by the appellant. She is
not able to tell the dates, it makes no difference. Perhaps,
she could not remember it. She is mentally retarded. She
may not perhaps be able to understand the details with
regard to date and time but, what had happened to her was
not something usual. Something unusual had happened to
her. She did remember it. She did remember it precisely.
She did tell that twice it was done. Her statement inspires
great confidence.
26. In fact, the victim was not able to understand the
consequences of the act which was done to her. Unaware of

14
the consequences of the act, still staying in the family
without complaining it to anyone. It is only when her mother
noticed her pregnancy that she revealed as to what had
happened to her. There were three women in the house, the
victim, her mother and her aunt. Her mother was a
Tuberculosis patient. When the PW1 brother of the victim
came to his village, he was told by his mother and aunt, as
to what had happened to the victim. It is thereafter he
lodged the FIR. The victim was already pregnant. On
10.08.2015, when she was examined, eight months foetus
was found in her womb.
29. The statement of PW2 victim finds corroboration
from the statement of PW3, her aunt and statement of PW1
her brother. The statements of these witnesses are reliable
and trustworthy. In fact, in the instant case, the statement
of PW2 the victim without any corroboration may be basis
for conviction.
30. An argument has been raised with regard to the
consensual sex. Merely because, the victim has stated in her
statement recorded under Section 164 of the Code that the
appellant would bring her roti, tobacco and mangoes, it
cannot be said that the act was consensual.

15
31. Section 114A of the Evidence Act, presumes
absence of consent in such acts. This Section is as
hereunder:-
"114A. Presumption as to absence of consent in
certain prosecution for rape. --In a prosecution for rape
under clause (a), clause (b), clause (c), clause (d), clause
(e), clause (f), clause (g), clause (h), clause (i), clause (j),
clause (k), clause (l), clause (m) or clause (n) of sub-section (2) of section 376 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of
1860), where sexual intercourse by the accused is proved
and the question is whether it was without the consent of
the woman alleged to have been raped and such woman
states in her evidence before the court that she did not
consent, the court shall presume that she did not consent.
Explanation.-- In this section, "sexual intercourse"
shall mean any of the acts mentioned in clauses (a) to (d)
of section 375 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860)."
32. In the instant case, the appellant has been
charged under Section 376 IPC The charge states that he
committed rape on the victim. It is not categorically stated
that the victim was mentally retarded. But, the victim has
been examined in the court as PW2 and the court has
observed that she is mentally retarded. The victim has been
cross examined by the prosecution. She stood the test of
cross examination. She has replied the answers in a most
rational manner. She categorically denied that she
established relations with the appellant willingly. She denied
for consent.

16
33. The appellant has been convicted under Section
376 (l) IPC. There is no Section as 376 (l) in IPC. It is, in
fact, Section 376 sub Section (2) (l) IPC, which provides for
punishment for rape on a woman suffering from mental or
physical disability. As stated, categorically Section 376 (2) (l)
IPC charge was not framed on the appellant. He was
charged under Section 376 IPC. The appellant throughout
knew as to who the victim is. The victim was examined and
the court observed that the victim is mentally retarded
woman. Therefore, the appellant since inception of the trial
knew that he is facing trial for committing rape on a woman,
who is mentally retarded. Therefore, merely because specific
charge under Section 376 (2) (l) is not framed on the
appellant, it does not vitiates the proceedings. In fact,
Section 464 of the Code makes provisions in this regard. It
is as hereunder:-
"464. Effect of omission to frame, or absence of,
or error in, charge.-(1) No finding, sentence or order by
a Court of competent jurisdiction shall be deemed invalid
merely on the ground that no charge was framed or on the
ground of any error, omission or irregularity in the charge
including any misjoinder of charges, unless, in the opinion
of the Court of appeal, confirmation or revision, a failure
of justice has in fact been occasioned thereby.
(2) If the Court of appeal, confirmation or revision,
is of opinion that a failure of justice has in fact been
occasioned, it may,-
(a) in the case of an omission to frame a charge,
order that a charge be framed, and that the

17
trial be recommended from the point
immediately after the framing of the charge;
(b) in the case of an error, omission or
irregularity in the charge, direct a new trial to
be had upon a charge framed in whatever
manner it thinks fit:
Provided that if the Court is of opinion that the facts
of the case are such that no valid charge could be
preferred against the accused in respect of the facts
proved, it shall quash the conviction."
34. In the instant case, the appellant has been
charged under Section 376 IPC for raping a woman, who
was mentally retarded. He has been convicted under Section
376 (l) IPC. It is an error. In fact, the appellant could have
been specifically charged under Section 376 (2) (l) IPC. But,
this error, in the charge does not vitiate the proceedings.
The appellant knew since inception the charge leveled
against him. Non framing of the charge under specific sub
section has not caused any failure of justice. It has not
effect.
35. Not only the oral evidence, but in fact, the
scientific evidence in the instant case proves that it is the
appellant, who committed rape on the victim. PW4 Sub
Inspector, Vinod Kumar, who conducted investigation has
stated about DNA samples. According to him, when dead
foetus was removed from the womb of the victim, the
hospital authorities did not take DNA samples. Therefore,

18
he applied in the court and the court requested the medical
authorities to take samples. The letter Ex. A4 has been
proved by PW4 Vinod Kumar. Not only this, according to
PW4 Vinod Kumar, he also applied in the court for taking
samples of the victim and thereafter, the court again
requested the concerned medical authorities for taking
samples of the appellant as well as the victim. These letters
Ex. A7 and A9 have been proved by this witness. According
to him, a Constable was sent to submit the samples in the
FSL. The FSL report dated 15.10.2015 is on record. It is Ex.
A14. PW4 Vinod Kumar has stated about these reports. FSL
report dated 15.10.2015 is submitted by the Assistant
Director, FSL, Dehradun. In view of Section 293 of the Code,
the report may be used as evidence in the trial. This report
concludes after examination as hereunder:-
"On the basis of above observations, it is concluded that:
1. Roshan Singh (source of exhibit-4 : Blood
sample) is the biological father of the Foetus
(source of exhibit-1 : : Placenta & exhibit-2 ;
Blood sample).
2. PW2, the victim (source of exhibit-7 : Blood
sample) is the biological mother of the Foetus
(source of exhibit-1 : : Placenta & exhibit-2 : Blood
sample)."
36. The statement of PW2 the victim proves the case
against the appellant. The statement of victim are supported
by the statements of her aunt and brother, who are PW3

19
and PW1 respectively. The FSL report further supports the
statement of the victim.
37. The matter may be examined from another
aspect. The appellant himself has never stated at any
occasion that the relationship was consensual. He has
simply denied. He denied of having any relationship with the
victim. Therefore, in view of the evidence, as adduced during
trial, this Court is of the view that the appellant established
physical relations with the victim without her consent.
38. An argument has been advanced that the FIR is
delayed. Delay in FIR is always not fatal for the prosecution.
In fact, in the cases of rape, it is a common phenomena that
the societal milieu restrains a person in promptly lodging an
FIR. After all, a person at times considers the consequences
of lodging an FIR. The social implications of it and
particularly, the future prospects of the victim. Instant is a
little different case. Here as stated, the victim, a woman of
39 years of age was staying in the village with her aunt. She
is mentally retarded. She never knew the consequences of
the act, which happened with her. She was not cautious.
She did not realize that she became pregnant. It is on asking
by her mother, she revealed as to what had happened to her
Thereafter, the report has been lodged. This report, even

20
cannot be termed as delayed and even if it is delayed, the
delay has been sufficiently explained. The delay does not
make the prosecution case in any manner doubtful.
39. In view of the foregoing discussion, this Court is
of the view that learned court below has rightly convicted
and sentenced the appellant of the charges under Sections
376 (2) (l) IPC. There is no reason to make any interference
in the impugned judgment and order. Accordingly, the
appeal deserves to be dismissed.
40. The appeal is dismissed.
41. Let a copy of this judgment along with Lower
Court Record be forwarded to the Court below for
compliance.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 08.12.2021
Jitendra
